# Artificial Intelligence Governance Professional (AIGP)

> A knowledge-based certification covering AI governance foundations, the laws and standards that apply to AI, and how to govern AI development, deployment and ongoing use.

**IAPP (International Association of Privacy Professionals)** · code `AIGP` · **$799 USD (non-member) / $649 USD (IAPP member). Retakes $625 / $475. Excludes the $250 certification maintenance fee per two-year term, waived by $295/year IAPP membership.** · 2 hours 45 minutes · pass 300 on a scaled 100-500 range (not a percentage) — 85 of the 100 questions are scored · valid 2 years, renewable with 20 CPE credits plus a maintenance fee or active membership · updated 2026-08-08

The AIGP is a governance credential. It tests whether you can navigate AI regulation, risk frameworks and life-cycle controls — not whether you can build, evaluate or secure a model. Read that sentence twice before you spend the money, because it is the whole decision.

## Where the weights come from

**The IAPP does not publish percentage weights.** It publishes something better: the Body of Knowledge gives a minimum and maximum question count per domain. The percentages above are SkillPilot's arithmetic on the official blueprint — the midpoint of each range, expressed as a share of the total.

That arithmetic is unusually well-grounded. The midpoints are 18, 21, 23 and 23, summing to 85 — exactly the number of scored questions the IAPP's candidate handbook states. Treat the percentages as reliable for study planning, but cite the question ranges, not our percentages, if precision matters.

## Your passing score is not a percentage

The exam is scaled 100–500, and 300 passes. **This is not 60%.** The scale maps raw correct answers onto a fixed range so that different exam forms are comparable, and the number of correct answers that lands on 300 varies. Fifteen of the 100 questions are unscored trial items you cannot identify. Do not budget your revision against "I need 60%" — you cannot know what the raw bar is.

## The cost is not the exam fee

This is the part most write-ups get wrong. The exam is $799, or $649 as a member. Passing does not make you certified: **the credential only becomes active once you hold IAPP membership or have paid a $250 certification maintenance fee**, and that repeats every two-year term. You also owe **20 CPE credits per term**, and letting either lapse suspends the credential and then revokes it.

Membership at $295/year covers the maintenance fee and cuts the exam price by $150, so buying membership first is usually cheaper than not. But be clear about what you are committing to: this is a subscription with an exam attached, not a one-off purchase. A failed first attempt is $625 non-member, $475 member.

## Who should actually buy this

Worth it if AI governance is your job or is becoming it — privacy and compliance professionals extending into AI, risk and legal teams, engineers who have moved into policy work or who sit on an AI review board, consultants who need the credential on a proposal. In those roles the vocabulary is the product, and the AIGP supplies it faster than reading the AI Act alone would.

Skip it if you build systems. It will not make you a better ML engineer, it does not prove you can secure a model, and no hiring manager will read it as evidence that you can. If your interest is adversarial robustness, evaluation or model security, your money goes further elsewhere.

## It is a young certification in a moving field

The AIGP launched in 2024 and the Body of Knowledge is already on version 2.1, restructured from seven domains to four. The IAPP reviews it annually and commits to 90 days' notice before new content appears. Regulation is moving faster than the syllabus, so verify the current BoK version yourself before you start studying — and expect the credential you renew in two years to test something different from the one you earn today.

## What the exam weights

The blueprint decides where study time goes. These are the published weights.

| Domain | Weight | |
|---|---:|---|
| Understanding how to govern AI development | 27% | `█████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░` |
| Understanding how to govern AI deployment and use | 27% | `█████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░` |
| Understanding how laws, standards and frameworks apply to AI | 25% | `█████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░` |
| Understanding the foundations of AI governance | 21% | `████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░` |

<details><summary><b>Understanding the foundations of AI governance</b> — 21%</summary>

- Generally accepted definitions and types of AI
- Risks and harms posed by AI to individuals, groups, organizations and society
- Common principles of responsible AI — fairness, safety, privacy, transparency, accountability
- Roles and responsibilities of AI governance stakeholders, and cross-functional collaboration
- Policies and procedures applied across every stage of the AI life cycle
- Differences among AI developers, providers, deployers and users

</details>

<details><summary><b>Understanding how laws, standards and frameworks apply to AI</b> — 25%</summary>

- How existing data privacy laws apply — lawful basis, purpose limitation, data minimization, DPIAs
- Nondiscrimination, consumer protection and product liability laws applied to AI
- Intellectual property limits on the use of data for AI training
- The EU AI Act risk classification — prohibited, high, limited and minimal risk
- Requirements for general-purpose AI models, enforcement and penalties
- The OECD AI Principles, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and ISO/IEC 22989, 42001 and 42005

</details>

<details><summary><b>Understanding how to govern AI development</b> — 27%</summary>

- Defining business context and performing impact assessments on an AI system
- Design and build governance — architecture and model selection, human oversight, operational controls
- Data governance, lawful rights to collect and use data, and data lineage and provenance
- Training and testing for performance, security, bias and interpretability
- Release readiness, model cards and conformity requirements
- Continuous monitoring, incident management, retraining and public transparency disclosures

</details>

<details><summary><b>Understanding how to govern AI deployment and use</b> — 27%</summary>

- Evaluating model types — classic versus generative, proprietary versus open source, multimodal
- Deployment options — cloud, on-premise, edge, fine-tuning, RAG and agentic architectures
- Vendor and licensing agreement terms and risks
- Applying policies to deployment — risk, issue management and user training
- Audits, red teaming, threat modeling and security testing of deployed systems
- Forecasting secondary and downstream harms, and controls to deactivate an AI system

</details>

## Before you book it

- No formal prerequisites — the IAPP does not require prior certification or experience
- Helpful, a working understanding of how machine learning systems are built and deployed
- Helpful, prior exposure to a regulatory or compliance framework such as GDPR

## How to prepare

6 steps, **about 67 hours** in total.

### 1. Download the Body of Knowledge and read the blueprint numbers

<sub>**~4 hours**</sub>

The BoK v2.1 is free, nine pages, and lists the minimum and maximum questions per domain. It is the exam's own specification. Read the performance indicators literally — the verbs (identify, understand, evaluate) tell you the depth each topic is tested at.

<details><summary><b>Resources</b> — 3, of which 3 free</summary>

- [AIGP Body of Knowledge and Exam Blueprint v2.1](https://prod.iapp.org/media/pdf/certification/AIGP_Cert_BOK_2025_FINAL_v2.1.0.pdf) <sub>IAPP · documentation · free</sub>
- [AIGP certification overview](https://iapp.org/certify/aigp) <sub>IAPP · certification · free</sub>
- [IAPP Certification Candidate Handbook](https://prod.iapp.org/media/pdf/certification/IAPP-Certification_Handbook_V5.3.1.pdf) <sub>IAPP · documentation · free</sub>

</details>

### 2. Learn the vocabulary of AI governance before the law

<sub>**~10 hours**</sub>

Domain I is definitions, principles and who is accountable for what. Get the developer/provider/deployer/user distinction straight first — it recurs throughout the legal domains, and every later question about obligations depends on correctly identifying which role you are in.

<details><summary><b>Resources</b> — 3, of which 3 free</summary>

- [OECD AI Principles](https://oecd.ai/en/ai-principles) <sub>OECD · documentation · free</sub>
- [What is an AI system? The OECD definition explained](https://oecd.ai/en/wonk/definition) <sub>OECD · documentation · free</sub>
- [IAPP AI Governance Center](https://iapp.org/ai-governance) <sub>IAPP · documentation · free</sub>

</details>

### 3. Work through the EU AI Act by risk tier

<sub>**~20 hours**</sub>

The Act is the single largest source of legal questions. Do not read it front to back. Learn the four risk tiers, what falls into each, and the specific obligations attached — then the general-purpose AI model rules, the enforcement regime and how duties differ by role.

<details><summary><b>Resources</b> — 3, of which 3 free</summary>

- [EU AI Act — high-level summary](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/high-level-summary/) <sub>EU AI Act (Future of Life Institute) · documentation · free</sub>
- [AI Act Explorer — full text by article and annex](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/ai-act-explorer/) <sub>EU AI Act (Future of Life Institute) · documentation · free</sub>
- [The AI Act — official text and translations](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/the-act/) <sub>EU AI Act (Future of Life Institute) · documentation · free</sub>

</details>

### 4. Learn the NIST AI RMF and the ISO standards by structure

<sub>**~12 hours**</sub>

The blueprint names NIST's four core functions and ISO/IEC 22989, 42001 and 42005 explicitly. Questions test structure and purpose, not clause detail — know what Govern, Map, Measure and Manage each cover, and which ISO standard does terminology, management systems and impact assessment.

<details><summary><b>Resources</b> — 3, of which 3 free</summary>

- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.100-1.pdf) <sub>NIST · documentation · free</sub>
- [NIST AI RMF Playbook](https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/playbook/) <sub>NIST · documentation · free</sub>
- [NIST AI Risk Management Framework overview](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework) <sub>NIST · documentation · free</sub>

</details>

### 5. Map the development and deployment domains onto real systems

<sub>**~18 hours**</sub>

Domains III and IV are 54% of the exam and are the most practical part of it. Take an AI system you know and walk it end to end: impact assessment, data provenance, testing, model card, release, monitoring, incident handling and deactivation. Abstract memorisation fails here.

<details><summary><b>Resources</b> — 2, of which 2 free</summary>

- [AIGP Body of Knowledge — Domains III and IV performance indicators](https://prod.iapp.org/media/pdf/certification/AIGP_Cert_BOK_2025_FINAL_v2.1.0.pdf) <sub>IAPP · documentation · free</sub>
- [NIST AI RMF Playbook — Map, Measure and Manage actions](https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/playbook/) <sub>NIST · documentation · free</sub>

</details>

### 6. Sort out the fees, then book

<sub>**~3 hours**</sub>

Decide on membership before you buy the exam, not after. Membership cuts the exam fee and covers the maintenance fee, so it usually pays for itself on the first sitting. Then confirm the CPE obligation you are signing up to for as long as you keep the credential.

<details><summary><b>Resources</b> — 4, of which 2 free</summary>

- [AIGP Exam — pricing and purchase](https://store.iapp.org/aigp-exam/) <sub>IAPP · certification · paid</sub>
- [Certification Maintenance Fee](https://store.iapp.org/certification-maintenance-fee/) <sub>IAPP · certification · paid</sub>
- [Stay certified — CPE requirements](https://iapp.org/certify/stay-certified) <sub>IAPP · documentation · free</sub>
- [IAPP Certification FAQs](https://iapp.org/certify/faqs) <sub>IAPP · documentation · free</sub>

</details>

## Questions

<details><summary><b>Does the AIGP certification teach you to build or secure AI systems?</b></summary><br>

No — the AIGP is a governance credential that tests whether you can navigate AI regulation, risk frameworks and life-cycle controls, not whether you can build, evaluate or secure a model. If your interest is adversarial robustness, evaluation or model security, this certification is not the right target.

</details>

<details><summary><b>How much does the AIGP exam actually cost once you include maintenance?</b></summary><br>

The exam itself is $799 non-member or $649 as an IAPP member, but passing does not make you certified: the credential only activates once you hold membership or pay a $250 maintenance fee every two-year term, plus 20 CPE credits per term. Membership at $295/year covers that fee and cuts the exam price by $150, so it usually pays for itself on the first sitting — a failed first attempt costs $625 non-member or $475 member to retake.

</details>

<details><summary><b>Is the AIGP passing score a percentage?</b></summary><br>

No. The exam is scaled from 100 to 500, and 300 passes — this is not 60%, because the scale maps raw correct answers onto a fixed range so different exam forms are comparable. Fifteen of the 100 questions are unscored trial items you cannot identify, so you cannot know what the raw score bar actually is.

</details>

<details><summary><b>What are the four AIGP exam domains and how are they weighted?</b></summary><br>

Understanding how to govern AI development and Understanding how to govern AI deployment and use are each 27% of the exam, together over half the content. The remaining weight splits between Understanding how laws, standards and frameworks apply to AI (25%) and Understanding the foundations of AI governance (21%), and these percentages come from SkillPilot's own arithmetic on the official Body of Knowledge question ranges, not an IAPP-published figure.

</details>

<details><summary><b>Who should actually get the AIGP certification?</b></summary><br>

It's worth it if AI governance is your job or is becoming it — privacy and compliance professionals extending into AI, risk and legal teams, engineers who have moved into policy work or sit on an AI review board, and consultants who need the credential on a proposal. Skip it if you build systems, since it will not make you a better ML engineer or prove you can secure a model.

</details>

<details><summary><b>Are there any prerequisites to sit the AIGP exam?</b></summary><br>

There are no formal prerequisites — the IAPP does not require prior certification or experience to register. It helps to have a working understanding of how machine learning systems are built and deployed, and prior exposure to a regulatory or compliance framework such as GDPR.

</details>
